chats.answer:
For a laptop with only one USB-C port, I'd recommend a laptop screen extender that supports video and power through a single USB-C cable.

The important distinction is whether you want one or two additional screens:

Single-screen extender: Best for portability, reliability, and minimal cable clutter.

Dual-screen extender: Gives you three screens total, but many models require two USB-C connections or additional HDMI/USB power cables.

My preference would be a single-screen extender with USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode support, unless you specifically need a triple-screen setup.

One thing to watch out for: a USB-C port doesn't necessarily support video output. The laptop must support DisplayPort Alt Mode, Thunderbolt, USB4, or an alternative such as DisplayLink.

chats.answer:
For a laptop with only one USB-C port, I'd recommend a laptop screen extender that supports HDMI + USB-A connections, or a USB-C extender with power pass-through.

The important thing is that you don't want your extender to occupy your only USB-C port and prevent you from charging your laptop.

What to look for

HDMI + USB-A support: Best if your laptop has an HDMI port and a USB-A port. HDMI carries video, while USB-A supplies power.

USB-C power pass-through: Lets you charge the laptop while using the screen, provided your laptop supports USB-C charging.

DisplayLink support: Useful when your USB-C port doesn't support video output or you want multiple extended displays.

Single-cable USB-C: Convenient, but only if the port supports DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt.
